page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 1 dedicated vCPU and 4 GB of system memory. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 1 physical core with 1 thread per core. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25% of tested servers. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory performance is a notable constraint, with both cached and uncached read-only memory bandwidth testing in the bottom 10%, and write bandwidth in the bottom 25%.

In application-specific workloads, the instance demonstrates average performance in single-threaded gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench text processing. Conversely, database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput fall into the bottom 10% of tested servers. For lightweight machine learning, the instance achieves an average text generation speed of 85.18 tokens per second on a small 135M parameter model, though prompt processing remains weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2d-standard-1 offers a low-cost entry point with dedicated CPU resources, avoiding the performance unpredictability of shared-core instances. However, the limited 4 GB memory capacity and lack of local storage present clear tradeoffs for resource-intensive applications. This instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, development environments, and simple background utility tasks that do not require high memory bandwidth or multi-core processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is an entry-level, general-purpose instance featuring 1 dedicated vCPU and 4 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 x86_64 processor. It provides a single physical core with 1 thread, 32 MB of L3 cache, and no local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests, though multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics fall into the bottom 10% to 25% cohorts. The instance achieves average results in single-threaded compression and text processing, but exhibits poor throughput for database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving. Qualitatively, it represents a highly cost-efficient option for dedicated compute resources at a minimal scale. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic utility scripts, and development environments.
